videos.script: A model scored on the rows it learned from will always look good. A tree in this lesson scores a perfect one on them. {{perfect}} On rows it has never seen, the same tree is the worst of six. {{worst}} So every honest score comes from rows held back. That is what a split is. {{split}} But holding rows back is not enough. They have to be held back from the right thing. {{right}} Here is a model that scores 0.994. Almost perfect. {{leak}} It got there by reading one column from a table that is rebuilt every night. The table knew who came back. The model learned to read the answer. {{table}} In production, that table can only know the past. And the same model flags four in five members as about to leave. {{prod}} That is leakage. Information from after the moment of prediction, in the rows that train or test the model. {{def}} This lesson finds it in three more places. Members who appear in two splits at once. Labels that are not finished yet. And preprocessing fitted on everything. {{three}} Each one is a data problem, not a modelling one. Which is why it is yours. {{yours}}
